title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this part of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' (the sequel to La Longue Marche), Grothendieck studies a large group 𝔖. It is apparently an extended modular or Teichmüller-type group acting on M, with a canonical surjection 𝔖→𝔖_3. The surrounding objects are: M, a modular-type group; Π_0, apparently a normal free-profinite (π_1 of the base) subgroup; M^!, a finite-index subgroup; a character ε_2: M→μ={±1}; and the subgroups M(0), M', M'', M^0. For elements ρ (order 3?) and τ', he forms centralisers Z_ρ and normalisers N_ρ^*.

The previous page (diagram (38)) listed four finite-index subgroups of Z_ρ: Z_ρ^! = M'(-j)×μ, Z_{ρ0}^! = M'(-j), M^0(-j)×μ and M^0(-j). The question is whether they are characteristic, or at least normal, in Z_ρ and in N_ρ^* = μ_{τ'}·Z_ρ.

This page:
(i) Z_ρ^! and M^0(-j)×μ are normal (even in N_ρ^*), being intersections of Z_ρ with M^! and Ker ε_2. These are subgroups stabilised by N_ρ^*.
(ii) Z_{ρ0}^! = M'(-j) has index 2 in Z_ρ^!. Since Z_ρ = L_ρ·Z_ρ^! with L_ρ generated by ρ, it suffices to show it is normalised by ρ. Normality inside Z_ρ^! is trivial because the subgroup has index 2.
(iii) He reduces this to a general question: when does x∈M (or 𝔖) normalise M_0^! := M(0)·Π_0? Since x normalises Π_0, it suffices that xux^{-1}∈M_0^! for u∈M(0). This is equivalent to xux^{-1}≡u mod Π_0, i.e. [x,u]∈Π_0.
(iv) He uses a previously established congruence (*): for x∈𝔖 and u∈M^!, [x,u] ≡ sg(x)^{ε_2(u)} mod Π_0. Here sg is the composite 𝔖→𝔖_3→μ (the signature).
(v) Lemma: for x∈𝔖^+ and u∈M_0^!, the following are equivalent: (a) xux^{-1}∈M_0^!; (b) [x,u]∈Π_0; (c) sg(x)^{ε_2(u)}=1, i.e. sg(x)=1 or ε_2(u) trivial.

The next page draws the conclusions. x normalises M_0^! iff sg(x)=+1. Since ρ has order 3, sg(ρ)=1, so all four subgroups are normal in Z_ρ. Normality under τ' requires computing the action of τ' on M'(-j)×μ.

The purpose is bookkeeping of the normaliser/centraliser structure of torsion elements in a modular-type group. This presumably serves the analysis of fixed points or finite subgroups in the Teichmüller tower and the 'loop equation' for Galois actions.
errors: The equivalence (a)⇔(b) silently uses that the image of M_0^! in M^!/Π_0 does not contain the nontrivial element of μ. Without this, xux^{-1}∈M(0)Π_0 does not imply xux^{-1}≡u mod Π_0. Given (*), the correction term lies in μ, so the claim holds once one knows −1∉M_0^!/Π_0; this is not stated.

Notational slip in (c): with ε_2 valued in μ={±1}, the expression sg(x)^{ε_2(u)} only makes sense if ε_2(u) is read additively in Z/2. In that reading, the condition 'ε_2(u)=1' should mean 'ε_2(u) trivial' (=0 additively, =+1 multiplicatively). As written, the exponent convention is ambiguous.
Minor: (*) is stated for u∈M^! but the lemma is for u∈M_0^!. This is consistent if M_0^!⊂M^!, which seems intended.

ideas.what: Criterion for an element of the extended modular group to normalise the finite-index subgroup M(0)·Π_0: the commutator with u is congruent mod Π_0 to the signature (via 𝔖→𝔖_3) raised to ε_2(u).
ideas.modern_name: Normaliser computation via a commutator/transfer-type character formula (signature character of 𝔖_3 composed with a mod-2 character)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard group theory; specific setting is Grothendieck's own

ideas.what: Determining which finite-index subgroups of the centraliser Z_ρ of a torsion element ρ are normal in Z_ρ and in the normaliser N_ρ^*.
ideas.modern_name: Centralisers/normalisers of finite-order elements in (profinite) mapping class / modular groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (e.g. Birman, Harvey, MacLachlan for mapping class groups); in the anabelian Teichmüller-tower context Grothendieck, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to the discussion of the Teichmüller tower in Esquisse d'un programme, but not at this level of detail

deep.surprise_reason: Routine group-theoretic verification (normality of index-2 subgroups via a commutator congruence) inside a larger unpublished computation. No new result or connection is visible on this page itself.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'Z^!_{ρ0} = M^!(-j)' should read Z^!_{ρ0} = M'(-j) (prime, not shriek), consistent with the previous page.
'comme si normalise Π_0' should read roughly 'comme x normalise Π_0'.
Under the commutator the annotation is 'x u(x)^{-1}' (a reminder of the commutator convention), not part of the formula.
In the lemma, the crossed-out word after 'alors' is replaced by 'conditions équivalentes'; part (c) has ε_2(u) written as a superscript exponent of sg(x).
